summary.headline: Prataap Snacks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to Rs 541 crore, but EBITDA fell to Rs 12.9 crore (2.4% margin) as input costs squeezed gross margin to 25.5%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations crossed Rs 500 crore for the first time, at Rs 541 crore (+26% YoY, +10% QoQ), with H1 revenue at Rs 1,031 crore (+23%). Gross margin fell to 25.5% from 29.8% a year ago, and EBITDA dropped to Rs 12.9 crore from Rs 22.9 crore; H1 EBITDA was Rs 32 crore. Management attributed the squeeze to palm oil, potato, packaging laminate, fuel and logistics inflation, partly offset by price hikes, grammage cuts and channel-margin changes. Management also announced a proposed Rs 421-422 crore greenfield plant near Indore and guided to a strong double-digit FY27 revenue growth.

segments.name: Namkeen
segments.commentary: Roughly 25% of revenue now, up from about 20% last year and 15-16% two years ago; leading growth, with manufacturing centralised in Indore and Rajkot.

segments.name: Extruded (Rings, Pellets)
segments.commentary: Extruded category about 39% of revenue: Pellets about 19-20%, Rings about 10%. Rings declined post-COVID; non-Rings grew at about 12% CAGR over 5-6 years.

segments.name: Potato chips
segments.commentary: Chips contribution reportedly rose to about 25% from 20% last quarter; available at about 30-35% of total outlet reach, with headroom.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Currently about 1.2-1.5% of sales; target about 5% of revenue over the next 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects strong double-digit revenue growth for FY27.
Targets H2 FY27 EBITDA margin similar to H1 level of around 3%.

Targets 5-6% margin benefit from levers: about 1.5-2 pp from new Indore plant (over ~1.5 years), 1.5-2% from channel margin, 1-1.5% from supply chain; medium term (2-3 years) target 9-10% EBITDA margin.
Medium-term targets cited on the call: 15% growth, 10% margin, 15% ROE.
New Indore plant internal target commissioning 1 January 2028 (realistically about 15 months); channel and supply-chain benefits to begin in a couple of quarters.
Another round of grammage rationalisation and price hikes planned in H2 due to further packaging laminate and corrugated price increases.
capex_capacity: Proposed greenfield plant near Indore on about 50 acres of leasehold industrial land from the state government; possession received in October 2026, and RLOP Foods (holding the leasehold rights) was acquired and will be merged into Prataap Snacks.

Project cost about Rs 421-422 crore, funded by roughly Rs 250 crore term loan plus internal accruals; interest rate below 8%. Debt to be prepaid from monetisation of existing Indore land valued at about Rs 250-300 crore.
New plant capacity about 65,000-70,000 metric tons, initially replicating existing lines, with room to double capacity without major land or building investment.
Existing Indore mother plant contributes about 40-45% of revenue, on about 14 acres with 7 smaller units in the same campus; phase 2 may consolidate Northern and Eastern operations.
demand_pricing: Transaction (packet) growth 17% and pricing growth 8-9% in Q2; management said volume and value growth are nearly the same.
MRP Rs 5 pack mix fell to 82% from 85% last year; Rs 10-20 packs rose to 14.5% of mix; quick commerce about 3.5% and modern trade/other large packs the remainder.
Reverse shift to packaged snacks from local players, who are struggling with palm oil and laminate supply; Prataap priced about Rs 4.15 vs about Rs 3.75 for local players on a similar Rs 5 product.

Distribution: about 2,200 primary distributors and about 3,000 sub-distributors, with direct and indirect reach around 2.5 million outlets; extruded at about 2 million outlets, Namkeen about 25% and chips 30-35% of total reach. Target 75% of current outlets for chips and Namkeen in 3-4 years.
Channel margin reduced from 14% to about 10.5% after eliminating super-stockists in 2022-23; about 2-2.5% headroom remains, being pulled selectively.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material volatility stabilise, and how is pricing power holding up with gross margin near 25-26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin fell about 8 pp from Q4 on input inflation, largely mitigated via price hikes, grammage and SKU optimisation; inefficiencies could add 5-6% margin.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new Indore plant's capacity, capex and land monetisation value?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity about 65,000-70,000 MT; project cost about Rs 421-422 crore with Rs 250-odd crore debt; existing land valued at Rs 250-300 crore to repay the term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP/ESAR charge in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50,000 ESARs granted with value of about Rs 5-6 crore, expensed over vesting of 4 years under Black-Scholes; about 2,300 shares allotted to employees on exercise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 125 crore short-term borrowing and the term loan rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term borrowing is about Rs 25 crore OD plus Rs 4 crore Jammu loan instalment; the new project term loan has not yet been drawn, with bulk drawdown next year, at under 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 margin trajectory given fresh inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Further packaging and corrugated inflation after Q2; management described a 9.5-10 pp gross-margin headwind vs pre-war Q4, with about 2.5% hitting operating profit, and said H2 EBITDA margin should be similar to H1 around 3%.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (palm oil, packaging laminate, corrugated, gas, freight) with further price and grammage moves needed in H2; consumer response to price hikes unknown.
Execution risk on the Rs 421-422 crore Indore greenfield plant and migration of existing lines; target commissioning 1 January 2028, realistically about 15 months.
Land monetisation of Rs 250-300 crore needed to prepay the term loan; timing not disclosed.
Gross margin recovery depends on channel-margin cuts and trade scheme changes, which could disrupt sales if pushed too fast.
Q2 EBITDA margin of 2.4% vs 2.4% needs to hold at about 3% in H2; quick commerce and new channels remain small, at about 1.2-1.5% of sales.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and distribution gains, but cautious on margins, with management acknowledging that input costs are still elevated and further price and grammage actions are needed. Answers on the ESOP cost, borrowing and the plant timeline were brief and some figures were corrected on the call.
key_quotes: Our gross margin for Q2 stood at 25.5% compared to 29.8% in the corresponding quarter last year.
We are available at more than 2.5 million outlets.
So, we expect about 1.5% to 2% we can get from the channel margin, including the distributor margin as well as some trade schemes, discounts, all put together.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H2 EBITDA margin targeted at about 3% (similar to H1, vs 2.4% in Q2), with 5-6 pp of levers cited: 1.5-2 pp from the new Indore plant (~1.5 years), 1.5-2% from channel margin (already cut from 14% to 10.5%, about 2-2.5% headroom left) and 1-1.5% from supply chain; medium-term target 9-10%, but a further 9.5-10 pp gross-margin headwind vs pre-war Q4 and about 2.5% hitting operating profit keeps near-term expansion uncertain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Greenfield Indore plant of 65,000-70,000 MT is firmly committed with possession received in October 2026 and an internal commissioning target of 1 January 2028 (realistically about 15 months), so it does not add capacity within the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Transaction (packet) volume grew 17% in Q2 with pricing up 8-9%, and management expects strong double-digit FY27 revenue growth; price hikes and grammage cuts planned in H2 could dent volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The Rs 421-422 crore Indore greenfield plant has already been announced, funded by about Rs 250 crore term loan (under 8%) plus internal accruals, with the new term loan not yet drawn and bulk drawdown next year; a further capex announcement is not signalled, though the plant can double capacity without new land.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 strong double-digit revenue growth and H2 EBITDA margin around 3%, but gross margin is 25.5% (vs 29.8%) with further inflation, so there is no basis for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was only 2.4% (Rs 12.9 crore vs Rs 22.9 crore), so H2 at about 3% needs gross margin recovery from price hikes and grammage cuts, and further laminate and corrugated increases are coming; the brief itself flags consumer response to price hikes as unknown.

rows.label: Channel-margin and supply-chain savings
rows.why: Channel margin cut from 14% to about 10.5% with 2-2.5% headroom left (1.5-2% margin benefit), and supply-chain benefit of 1-1.5% expected to begin within a couple of quarters.

rows.label: Further price hikes and grammage cuts in H2
rows.why: Another round planned due to further laminate and corrugated increases; Q2 pricing growth was 8-9% and a 9.5-10 pp gross-margin headwind vs pre-war Q4 is still being offset.

rows.label: Land monetisation to prepay term loan
rows.why: Indore land valued at Rs 250-300 crore is to repay the roughly Rs 250 crore term loan, but timing is not disclosed and the project's term loan is not yet drawn.
